I think recursive discovery and multi-skill selection are two separate things.

Recursive discovery may already be partially implemented depending on the expected `SKILL.md` structure.

The main UX pain for me is multi-skill selection from `/skills`.

Instead of typing:

```txt
/use auth,database
```

I think a better UX would be:

```txt
/skills
```

Then:

- `Space` toggles skills
- `Enter` applies selected skills
- Prompt shows `[2 skills selected]`
- Selected skills are injected as context on submit
- Selection clears after submit

This solves the real use case: applying multiple skills to one prompt without chaining slash commands manually.

Rebased onto current `dev` (`f692d536b`) — mergeable and green again. Both bugs are still live on `dev`:

- **#26929** — `OutputFormatText` / `OutputFormatJsonSchema` in `packages/core/src/v1/session.ts` are still `Schema.Class`, so encoding a plain DB row crashes `GET /session/:id/message` (it serializes via `SessionV1.WithParts`). Converted both to `Schema.Struct`, matching the rest of the file.
- **#25430** — `prompt.ts` still constructs `StructuredOutputError` with a hardcoded `retries: 0`. This wires `format.retryCount` (default 2): on a structured-output miss, the loop persists a synthetic `<system-reminder>` and re-runs the step with `toolChoice: "required"` still in force, then reports the real count when it finally gives up.

One note re: my earlier offer to retarget — the new v2 session runtime (`packages/core/src/session/`) has no structured-output support yet (no `format` field, no synthetic `StructuredOutput` tool, no `toolChoice`), so v1 is still the only path this affects. Happy to keep it rebased, or to close if you'd rather fold these into a v2 effort.

I told an agent to look through the opencode source to answer this. Can't guarantee its accuracy but hope it might be helpful.

Session logs (commands + outputs) are stored in:

%LOCALAPPDATA%\opencode\opencode.db — a SQLite database containing every session, message, tool call (including all bash commands and their outputs)

%LOCALAPPDATA%\opencode\tool-output\ — large command outputs that got truncated (>2000 lines or 50KB)

%LOCALAPPDATA%\opencode\log\opencode.log — app-level structured logs

Recovery: If %LOCALAPPDATA%\opencode\ still exists, your data is likely intact since opencode's data is separate from its npm install. You can:

1. Reinstall opencode (`npm install -g opencode-ai` after reinstalling node.js, or download the desktop app installer from opencode.ai)
2. Run `opencode session list` to see all sessions
3. Or open opencode.db with any SQLite browser (or tell any agent to analyze it) — the message table has JSON blobs containing every command and its output

Note: %LOCALAPPDATA% is usually C:\Users\<YourUsername>\AppData\Local. You can test it in CMD with `echo %LOCALAPPDATA%`

This seems to address the underlying cause of the issue I reported.

My original concern was that, after context compaction, the model would forget previous failed attempts and repeat the same solution multiple times. The proposed changes explicitly mention preserving debugging state, tested hypotheses, ruled-out approaches, and the evidence behind those conclusions, which should prevent that behavior.

Since this feature request covers the broader problem of information loss during compaction, I believe my issue is sufficiently addressed here. Closing in favor of this request.
